source: Lake & Baroni (2018) Generalization without Systematicity (SCAN)
finding: Seq2seq RNNs generalize on random splits but fail on systematic recombination. A 'jump' primitive learned alone does not combine with 'twice', 'left' and so on.
numbers: Random 80/20 split: best net 99.8%. Training on 2% of commands: about 54%; 4%: about 93%. Length split: best 13.8% (20.8% to 23.6% with oracle or tuned variants). Add-jump split: best 1.2% (best overall model 0.08%); turn-left split: up to 90.3%. Five runs each.
limits: Small synthetic grammar. Success on 'turn left' but failure on 'jump' shows the result depends on how often the primitive appears inside composed contexts (turn left was over-represented, roughly 10% of training).
agent_relevance: Rule and primitive recombination is not free in plain learned sequence models. The scaffold should state rules explicitly.

source: Hupkes et al. (2020) Compositionality decomposed (PCFG SET)
finding: Splits 'compositionality' into five tests: systematicity, productivity, substitutivity, localism, overgeneralisation. Tests LSTM, ConvS2S and Transformer on one grammar.
numbers: Task accuracy LSTM 0.79, ConvS2S 0.85, Transformer 0.92. Systematicity 0.53 / 0.56 / 0.72. Productivity (longer than seen) 0.30 / 0.31 / 0.50. Overgeneralisation 0.68 / 0.79 / 0.88. Three runs each.
limits: One synthetic grammar. Architecture ranking is data-set specific. Productivity is weakest for all three, in line with Fodor's productivity argument.
agent_relevance: Gives a vocabulary for what to test in the agent: recombination, length extrapolation, synonym robustness, local vs global composition.

source: Keysers et al. (2020) Measuring compositional generalization (CFQ, SCAN MCD)
finding: Maximum compound divergence (MCD) splits keep atoms equal but change how atoms combine. All tested neural parsers collapse on them.
numbers: CFQ random vs MCD: LSTM+attention 97.4 vs 14.9; Transformer 98.5 vs 17.9; Universal Transformer 98.0 vs 18.9. SCAN MCD: 6.1, 1.1, 1.2. Compound divergence explains accuracy with R2 0.81-0.88; length ratios give R2 0.11-0.22.
limits: Pre-LLM baselines. Later work shows large gains from better configs and prompts (b05, b07).
agent_relevance: Failure tracks novelty of combinations, not length or atom novelty. Check agent tasks for unseen combinations of known pieces.

source: Kim & Linzen (2020) COGS
finding: Semantic parsing benchmark with 21 generalization cases (new roles for known words, deeper recursion). In-distribution is near perfect, generalization is poor.
numbers: Dev/test about 0.96-0.99 for LSTMs and Transformer; generalization set: Transformer 0.35 (sd 0.06), uni-LSTM 0.32, bi-LSTM 0.16. Recursion-depth cases near 0%. 1000 examples per each of 21 cases (21,000 total).
limits: High variance across seeds. Structural generalization (recursion, PP depth) is much harder than lexical.
agent_relevance: Depth and recursion extrapolation is the hardest case. A model that handles depth 2 may fail at depth 5.

source: Csordas, Irie & Schmidhuber (2021) The Devil is in the Detail
finding: Failure of baseline Transformers was partly a configuration artifact. Embedding scaling, early stopping on a generalization split, relative position embeddings and Universal Transformer variants raise scores a lot.
numbers: PCFG productivity split 50% to 85%; PCFG systematicity 72% to 96%; COGS 35% to 81%; SCAN length split (cutoff 26) reaches 100% with relative positions. Differences are invisible on IID validation data.
limits: Still tuned per benchmark. Needs a held-out generalization validation set, which is rarely available in real use.
agent_relevance: A negative systematicity result can be a weak baseline. Weigh 'models cannot do X' claims by baseline quality.

source: Ontanon et al. (2022) Making Transformers Solve Compositional Tasks
finding: Position encoding, decoder type, weight sharing and target format change compositional generalization a lot across 12 datasets. Some tasks do not improve at all.
numbers: State of the art on COGS and PCFG at the time; twelve datasets, six standard plus algorithmic tasks (addition, duplication, set intersection). Per-dataset numbers not extracted.
limits: Abstract and introduction read only.
agent_relevance: Inductive bias, not only scale, sets systematicity. Supports a scaffold that supplies structure.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Least-to-most prompting
finding: Decomposing a problem into ordered subproblems lets a prompted LLM solve SCAN splits from 14 exemplars, closing a gap that trained seq2seq nets could not.
numbers: SCAN length split: code-davinci-002 least-to-most 99.7% vs chain-of-thought 16.2% (standard prompting 16.7%). Same prompt at 99% or more on every SCAN split. Chain-of-thought reached 37.4% in one length-12 setting with 4 exemplars.
limits: SCAN is a clean toy grammar. Needs a hand-written decomposition prompt and a code-trained model.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that an explicit decomposition operator restores productivity. Maps to a decompose-then-solve step in the schema.

source: Press et al. (2023) Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap
finding: LLMs answer single facts but fail to compose two of them. Scaling raises both but not the gap.
numbers: Compositionality gap stays about 40% across GPT-3 sizes (Compositional Celebrities, 8.6k 2-hop questions). Self-ask 79.6% vs 45.7% for chain-of-thought with InstructGPT-Davinci-002 on CC; Davinci 54.2% vs 1.1%. Cited later checks: ChatGPT gap 42.9%, GPT-4 23.0%.
limits: Gap fell in GPT-4 but did not vanish. One question type.
agent_relevance: Make the agent ask and answer sub-questions explicitly, then combine. Measure the gap on its own knowledge.

source: Dziri et al. (2023) Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
finding: Transformers appear to solve compositional tasks by matching linearized subgraphs seen in training, not by learning the algorithm. Error grows with computation-graph depth.
numbers: 3-digit by 3-digit multiplication zero-shot: ChatGPT 55%, GPT-4 59%. In 4-digit by 2-digit multiplication (unseen size) 82.3% of final-correct answers still had at least one wrong step in the graph. Accuracy falls toward zero beyond the fine-tuned problem size; training past overfitting gave no OOD gain.
limits: Tested GPT-3 fine-tuning plus theory; later frontier models improved with tools and reasoning traces.
agent_relevance: Do not trust final-answer accuracy alone. Verify intermediate steps and use code or tools for exact symbol manipulation.

source: Lake & Baroni (2023) Human-like systematic generalization through meta-learning (MLC)
finding: A standard Transformer trained over many episodes of fresh few-shot compositional tasks reaches human-level systematicity, with human-like errors. This answers Fodor and Pylyshyn with a training regime, not symbolic hardware.
numbers: Humans 80.7% exact match on algebraic-standard answers, 72.5% on longer outputs. MLC 82.4% and 77.8%. Errors on function 3: one-to-one 24.4% of human errors vs 56.3% MLC; iconic concatenation 23.3% vs 13.8%. SCAN error: add-jump 0.22% vs 99.27% plain seq2seq; around-right 0.04% vs 51.13%; opposite-right 0.06% vs 100%; COGS lexical 0.87% vs 6.08%. Averages of five runs.
limits: The training distribution is built to teach compositional use; it does not show systematicity appears without it. Pseudo-language with a small vocabulary.
agent_relevance: Practice on many small compositional tasks can instil systematic behavior. The scaffold can use few-shot episodes for rule use.

source: Berglund et al. (2023) The Reversal Curse
finding: A model trained on 'A is B' does not infer 'B is A'. The likelihood of the right answer is no higher than for a random name. Given in context, the reverse works.
numbers: Finetuned GPT-3 on fictitious facts: about 96.7% in the trained order, near 0% in reverse, across a hyperparameter sweep. Real celebrities, GPT-4: parent question 79%, reverse child question 33% (1573 pairs, 10 samples each).
limits: Parametric memory only. Real-world estimate may be low because of refusals.
agent_relevance: Knowledge is not stored as a reusable relation. Put key facts in context and ask in both directions.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Reasoning or Reciting? Counterfactual tasks
finding: Moving a task to a counterfactual rule set (base-9 arithmetic, altered chess rules, shifted indexing, altered word order) lowers GPT-4 and other models across 11 tasks, though above chance.
numbers: Eleven tasks, default vs counterfactual conditions. Direction consistent: counterfactual below default. Per-task values not extracted.
limits: Abstract and design read only. Counterfactual tasks may be harder for reasons beyond memorization.
agent_relevance: Test the agent on rule variants. Success on the default rule may be recall.

source: McCoy et al. (2024) Embers of Autoregression
finding: LLM accuracy depends on probability of the task, the output and the input, even for deterministic symbolic tasks where probability should not matter.
numbers: Shift cipher, GPT-4: 51% when output is high-probability text, 13% when low. Shift levels 1, 3, 13 above 50%, other shifts under 3%. Pig Latin 42% common variant vs 23% rare. Some control tasks near ceiling (99.8% GPT-3.5, 99.9% GPT-4). Eleven tasks, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.
limits: Older models. Newer reasoning models may reduce the effect.
agent_relevance: Symbol-like operations are done statistically. Unusual inputs and outputs are risky and must be checked.

source: Lampinen et al. (2024) Language models show human-like content effects on reasoning
finding: On NLI, syllogisms and the Wason task, LMs reason better when content supports the logic, as people do. Content-independent abstract reasoning is not the default.
numbers: Cited human baseline: people mistakenly accepted belief-consistent invalid syllogisms about 90% of the time. Model-human parallels reported with bootstrap 95% CIs. Exact accuracy gaps not extracted.
limits: Abstract and introduction read. Human-like imperfection is not proof of a missing symbolic system.
agent_relevance: Rival reading: human reasoning is also content-bound. Calibrate how formal the agent can be.

source: Webb, Holyoak & Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: GPT-3 zero-shot matches or beats UCLA undergraduates on abstract relational problems, which counts against the claim that variable-like abstraction needs built-in symbols.
numbers: Digit matrices: GPT-3 beat humans (N=40): generative OR 1.88, p=0.005; multiple choice OR 6.27, p=2.3e-8. Other samples: letter string N=57, verbal analogies N=57, story analogies N=54.
limits: Possible training-data exposure. Text-only tasks.
agent_relevance: Relational abstraction can emerge. Still test on altered versions.

source: Gendron et al. (2023) Large Language Models Are Not Strong Abstract Reasoners
finding: Wide benchmark shows weak abstract reasoning; fine-tuning improves in-distribution but fails on out-of-distribution syntax.
numbers: GPT-4 and Text-Davinci-3 improve with number of examples, up to about 0.6 accuracy at 16 examples. Fine-tuned LLaMA2 reaches near-perfect test accuracy but drops significantly on the OOD splits.
limits: 2023 models. Per-benchmark values not extracted.
agent_relevance: Few examples help; fine-tuning does not transfer across syntax.

source: Feng & Steinhardt (2024) How do language models bind entities in context?
finding: Mechanistic evidence for a variable-binding-like code: LMs attach binding ID vectors to entities and attributes. Interventions swap their beliefs.
numbers: Additivity check: accuracy above 99% for Control and below 3% for Attribute and Entity mean interventions. Found in every sufficiently large Pythia and LLaMA model.
limits: Small synthetic contexts. Binding distances reflect how discernible entities are, so capacity is limited.
agent_relevance: LLMs can host symbol-like variables in activations. Keep the number of tracked entities small.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Grokked Transformers are Implicit Reasoners
finding: Transformers learn two-hop composition only by grokking (training far past fitting), and still fail out-of-distribution composition, though they succeed at comparison.
numbers: Train accuracy above 99% at about 14K steps while ID test was 9.2%; ID near perfect after about 50 times more steps. OOD composition stayed at zero after 2 million steps. A fully grokked model is near perfect on a large-search task where GPT-4-Turbo and Gemini-1.5-Pro fail.
limits: Synthetic facts. Proposed fix (cross-layer sharing) not tested at scale.
agent_relevance: Composition of stored facts is the weak spot, so retrieve then compose in context.

source: Fodor & Pylyshyn (1988) Connectionism and cognitive architecture
finding: Founding argument: thought is productive and systematic, so mental representations need combinatorial syntax and structure-sensitive operations; connectionist nets either implement this or fail.
numbers: No empirical numbers. Argument from productivity, systematicity, compositionality and inferential coherence.
limits: Not opened this session; from background knowledge. Empirical tests came later (b01-b10).
agent_relevance: The argument predicts the failures in b01-b09; b10 is the live counterexample.

source: Marcus (1998) Rethinking eliminative connectionism
finding: Argues that nets fail to generalize outside the training space and need variable-like operations. Fits the later SCAN results.
numbers: No numbers recorded.
limits: Not opened. Background knowledge.
agent_relevance: Historical anchor for the extrapolation critique.

source: Fodor & McLaughlin (1990) Connectionism and the problem of systematicity
finding: Reply to Smolensky: tensor-product schemes do not make constituents causally active, so they do not explain systematicity.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Frames what counts as a real systematic process versus an implemented one.

source: Quilty-Dunn, Porot & Mandelbaum (2023) The best game in town: the re-emergence of the language-of-thought hypothesis
finding: Gathers evidence from vision, animal cognition and infants for discrete, abstract, compositional representations and treats LoT as the best empirical theory, with testable signatures.
numbers: No numbers recorded. Signatures: discrete constituents, role-filler independence, predicate-argument structure, logical operators, inferential promiscuity, abstract content.
limits: Not opened. Commentaries in the same issue dispute whether neural nets already show the signatures.
agent_relevance: Gives a checklist of LoT signatures to test in an LLM scaffold.

source: Newman, Hewitt, Liang & Manning (2020) The EOS decision and length extrapolation
finding: Length failure on SCAN is partly the model not learning when to stop, not purely a failure to compose. Cited by Csordas et al. (b05) as the 'EOS decision problem'.
numbers: No direct numbers read.
limits: Secondary citation only.
agent_relevance: Length failures may come from the stopping decision, a separable fault.

source: Dehaene, Al Roumi, Lakretz, Planton & Sable-Meyer (2022) Symbols and mental programs
finding: Argues humans, unlike other primates, compress sequences and shapes into short programs over primitives (a language of geometry), so program length predicts human difficulty.
numbers: No numbers recorded.
limits: Not opened. Human side only.
agent_relevance: A program-like internal plan is a reasonable scaffold design.

source: Synthesis of b08 and b13 (not a new source)
finding: Dziri and McCoy both show failures that scale with rarity or size of the structure rather than with its logical difficulty. This fits a statistical account with partial rule-like circuits (b17).
numbers: From b08: 82.3% of correct 4x2-digit answers had a wrong intermediate step. From b13: GPT-4 cipher 51% vs 13% by output probability.
limits: Synthesis only.
agent_relevance: Rival theories separate on counterfactual and low-probability variants, not default benchmarks.

source: Synthesis of b01, b07, b10 (not a new source)
finding: Three routes reach near-perfect SCAN: symbolic components (cited in b05), meta-learning (b10, 99.78% or more) and prompted decomposition (b07, 99.7%). Plain trained nets stay at 0.08%-1.2% on add-jump.
numbers: SCAN add-jump: plain seq2seq error 99.27% vs MLC 0.22%; prompts 99.7% on length split.
limits: Synthesis only. Solved benchmarks may not transfer (Csordas notes limited gains elsewhere).
agent_relevance: Systematicity looks like a property of training or scaffolding, not architecture alone.
